answer: A claim token's neighbourhood is what this ledger pays for: no rival may occupy a token within three slots, and two identities seated inside each other's span forfeit both escrows, while a lone agent takes any free seat. Each epoch mints a fixed ring, so a farm must space its k names pairwise apart. Its first seat is trivial; its tenth wants a ten-slot buffer, and as k rises the ring tightens until the marginal seat costs more than it earns. The yarrow marks one stalk per holder, the velvet burns on any collision, and an orchard ten strong can be planted where a hundred aliases cannot.
